cards.sig: the station has got / gotten a lot nicer. also fine: has become a lot nicer the station · nice they renovated it last year a place near you that has got / gotten a lot nicer — or a lot worse. what happened?

tvs are a lot cheaper than they used to be. also fine: tvs have got / gotten a lot cheaper. tvs · cheap you pay much less now than twenty years ago two things that are a lot cheaper — or a lot more expensive — than they used to be. which one do you notice most?
the summers are getting hotter and hotter. the summers · hot every year it’s worse two things that are getting better and better — or worse and worse — where you live. which one matters most to you?

my favourite restaurant isn’t as good as it used to be. also fine: … isn’t as good as it was. my favourite restaurant · good it was better ten years ago a café, a shop or a tv show that isn’t as good as it used to be. what’s changed?

the old town has become a lot more touristy. also fine: … is a lot more touristy than it used to be. the old town · touristy souvenir shops everywhere now a place that has become a lot more touristy — or one that hasn’t changed at all. why do you think that is?
my street is getting noisier and noisier. my street · noisy a new bar opens every month what’s getting more and more popular where you live? who’s happy about it, and who isn’t?

at first, i enjoyed at first, i enjoyed the novelty of it. ___ the novelty of it. in the beginning, i liked it — everything was new and exciting. first in the beginning, i liked how new it was · поначалу мне нравилась новизна · also fine: at first, i liked…

no matter where no matter where i went, the first night was always hard. ___ i went, the first night was always hard. wherever i went, the first night was always hard. matter wherever i went · куда бы я ни поехал

the problem was the problem was, i had nobody to talk to. ___, i had nobody to talk to. but there was one thing i didn't like: i had nobody to talk to. problem the catch was… · проблема была в том, что…

hit me like a ton of bricks when i got home, the loneliness hit me like a ton of bricks. when i got home, the loneliness ___. when i got home, i suddenly felt terribly lonely. bricks i suddenly felt it very strongly · накрыло (как обухом по голове)

time on my hands after i stopped working, i had a lot of time on my hands. after i stopped working, i had a lot of ___. after i stopped working, i had lots of free time and nothing to fill it with. hands free time and nothing to fill it with · свободное время, которое нечем занять

get out of the house i need to get out of the house and go somewhere — anywhere. i need to ___ and go somewhere — anywhere. i can't stay at home all day — i need to go somewhere, anywhere. out leave home, don't stay stuck indoors · выбраться из дома · not go out: go out = usually for fun
makes me feel part of something my choir makes me feel part of something. my choir ___. when i sing in my choir, i feel like i really belong. part i feel i belong · чувствовать себя частью чего-то

you name it i fill my days with all sorts of things: books, films, cooking, gardening — you name it. i fill my days with all sorts of things: books, films, cooking, gardening — ___. i fill my days with all sorts of things: books, films, cooking, gardening and lots more. name all kinds of things · чем я только не занимаюсь

can't explain it there's a little café on my street. can't explain it, but i like it there. there's a little café on my street. ___, but i like it there. there's a little café on my street. i don't know why, but i like it there. explain i don't know why · не могу объяснить почему · also fine: i can't explain it
i've tried everything believe me, i've tried everything. believe me, ___. honestly, there's nothing i haven't tried. everything i've tried it all → present perfect: a sum-up to now · всё перепробовал

excuse me, mind if i sit here? no, go ahead. a busy café. a woman with a coffee points at the free chair at your table. thanks! it's so busy today. mind if i…? = do you mind if i…? · вы не против, если я…? · no = i don't mind · я не против
mind if i open the window? no, not at all. it's really hot in here. a hot train. the man next to you looks at the window. thanks — that's much better. no, not at all. = нет, что вы, пожалуйста.
mind if i borrow your pen? no, not at all — here you go. at work. a colleague needs your pen for a second. thanks, i'll give it right back. here you go = вот, держи
